method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

verification_summary.limitation: Selected source access and manually adjudicated record-level passages are listed separately. Verification applies only to individually listed claims; all remaining evidence/pathways and the country bank as a whole remain unresolved-limited.

source_refs.locator: NDC summary, PDF p. 3.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2021 NDC describes the Kyrgyz Republic as highly climate-vulnerable and reliant on climate-sensitive sectors; disasters, disease, infrastructure damage, and reduced water can threaten development, energy, and irrigation.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The NDC says women and children in rural households carry much of the work of obtaining domestic water and fuel, while women face barriers to finance, training, technology, and climate decision-making.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.scenario: The NDC cites water-availability decline over 2050-2100; the conflict-risk statement does not specify an emissions scenario.

recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: FAO feature story, Ak-Bashat farmer account

evidence.compact_statement: FAO's May 2024 feature links stream drying in Ak-Bashat to climate change; one farmer describes switching from orchards to cattle and water depletion causing disputes.
